四级核心词汇 · 08英文原文

The Voice Beneath the Article

文章下面的那段声音 · 600 词 · 8 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1Ari, an undergraduate, enrolled in a journalism class. The curriculum required an article about an ordinary person at work. She chose a woman who ran a repair stall near campus. She greeted Ari in a warm tone, with the distinct rhythm of her dialect. She called her tools old-fashioned and laughed. The editor quoted only that phrase in the headline of the first edition. At the stall the next morning, the woman refused to read any further.

2Ari asked why the words had sounded harsh. The woman said the quotation implied that she was ashamed of her occupation. Ari played the recording. Before making the remark, the woman had shown her a hammer that belonged to her father. That tool still did a job a contemporary substitute could not do. The praise was clear in her tone. In print, one phrase had conveyed the opposite attitude.

3A faculty adviser asked them to underline the key words and define each. A fluent speaker could infer the implicit praise from the laugh. A reader could only interpret the words on the page. The adviser asked Ari to make the account more coherent. She moved the hammer beside the quotation in the layout and added one sentence to explain the context. The change gave the account coherence.

4A fellow pupil suggested an audio clip to engage readers. The editor worried that traffic noise would interrupt comprehension. Ari chose a short segment and wrote a transcript. A retired scholar checked the literal definition of two dialect words. One had no counterpart in standard English. Instead of imitating the accent, Ari added a note about it. She sought consent and confirmed the surname's spelling before the edit.

5A student wanted to cite an online post that attributed the mistake to bias. Was it relevant? Ari could not find a reliable source for that claim. She asked the class to compare the composition with the recording. One pupil had assumed a short quotation could represent a conversation. Another described how a heading influenced a reader's viewpoint. They drew arrows to relate each claim to its source and highlight gaps. The changes improved cohesion without adding much length.

6The department asked Ari to compose a guideline for its next project. She explained the difference between an exact quotation and a fair summary. A writer could omit a repeated word. An omission that changed the meaning needed another approach. She added an instruction about copyright and a thoughtful example of how to ask for consent. The teacher recommended its practical format for an elementary course on academic writing.

7A blind student offered to test the audio and the text separately. He could comprehend the laugh without seeing the article. The recording, however, needed an introduction to identify the speaker. Ari and the editor collaborated on a short spoken greeting. The collaboration made communication clearer for anybody who began with audio. A trial broadcast revealed one more problem. In the spoken script, the conjunction connecting the woman's two remarks was missing. Ari restored it so the two remarks fit together naturally. It changed the implication of the first. The next listener could follow both statements without seeing the hammer.

8When the revised feature appeared on the Internet, the woman clicked the recording and placed the hammer beside the screen. A customer asked if the author had believed some gossip. The woman said the words were accurate. What changed was their relation to the story. Then she showed Ari a second tool and offered to explain why it was worth keeping. Ari recorded the sentence before the laugh this time.

四级核心词汇 · 08中文译文

文章下面的那段声音

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1本科生阿里选了一门新闻课。课程要求写一篇文章，讲一个普通人怎样工作。她选了在学校附近摆维修摊的女士。女士亲切地向她打招呼，说话带着本地方言特有的节奏。她笑着说自己的工具老式。编辑在第一版标题里只引了那几个字。第二天早上，女士在摊上看到文章，就不想再读下去了。

2阿里问，为什么那句话听着刺耳。女士说，那段引文让人以为她为自己的职业难为情。阿里播放录音。原来在说那句话之前，女士先给她看了一把父亲留下的锤子。新工具干不了的活，这把旧锤子还能做。她语气里明明是赞赏，单独印出那几个字，却传达了相反的态度。

3系里的一位指导老师请大家把关键词画出来，逐个解释。听得懂方言的人能从笑声里听出没明说的赞美，只看文章的人只能从页面上的词来理解。老师请阿里把前后接得更连贯。她把锤子的描述挪到引文旁，加一句话交代语境。这样，读者就能看出前后之间的联系。

4一名同学建议加段录音，让读者也参与进来。编辑担心车声太大会妨碍理解。阿里选了一小段，把它写成文字。一位退休学者核对了两个方言词的字面意思。其中一个在标准英语里没有完全对应的词。阿里没有刻意模仿口音，只加了一句说明。改稿前，她征得女士同意，也核实了女士姓氏的拼法。

5一个学生想引用网上的帖子，说这次失误源于偏见。这条消息跟问题有关吗？阿里找不到可信的出处来支持这种说法，就请同学把文章和录音对照。有同学原先以为，一小段引文可以代表整次谈话。另一个说，标题会影响读者看事情的角度。他们用箭头把每个说法连到它的来源，标出证据没接上的地方。文章没有长多少，前后却接得更紧了。

6系里请阿里给下一次项目写一份指引。她讲清了逐字引用和公允概括的区别。重复的话可以省掉，省略会改变意思时就得换个做法。她加了一条版权说明，还举了一个体贴的例子，教大家怎样征得受访者同意。老师觉得格式实用，推荐给入门的学术写作课。

7一名视障学生主动提出把音频和文字分开测试。他听得懂那声笑，但录音需要先说明说话人是谁。阿里和编辑合作写了几句口头介绍，让从录音开始听的人更容易跟上。试播时他们又发现一个问题，讲稿漏了连接女士两句话的连词。阿里把它补回去，两句话自然接到一起，第一句的言外之意也变了。下一位试听的人即使看不到锤子，也能听懂这两句话。

8修改后的报道发到网上。女士点开录音，把锤子放在屏幕旁。一个顾客问，作者是不是听信了什么闲话。女士说，话本身是准确的，改变的是那句话在整个故事里的位置。接着，她给阿里看了第二件工具，愿意讲讲为什么值得留下。这一次，阿里也录下了笑声前的那句话。
